formal.anchor: A dimension is a semantic axis of variation or classification along which statements about an observation can be made ... d=RelationshipToArjuna with possible values V_d={grandfather, teacher, brother, friend, ...} ... s=(Bhishma,d,grandfather) is a statement, not a dimension.

governance.anchor: We should not move to Phase 3 yet. We have just discovered something important about the ordering: before defining the relationship between Zero, Lord and Sārathi, we should finish defining the knowledge primitives—especially Dimension

lexical.anchor: Give me your understanding of Dimension first. We will then put it through Lord + Zero + Krishna + DDD + Gita, and only afterwards formalize it mathematically.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Before observation: Enemy. After observation: Enemy ∩ Relative ∩ Teacher ∩ Elder. This is not merely adding dimensions. It is reorganizing the relationship structure.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues Arjuna's Selection S was not merely adding new selected dimensions but restructuring relationships among existing ones (Enemy alone becoming Enemy-intersect-Relative-intersect-Teacher-intersect-Elder), supporting the principle NewKnowledge -> Reinterpretation(ExistingKnowledge), with the earlier 'Enemy' representation reframed as incomplete rather than false (a Zero-Lens-style move).

rationale_evidence.anchor: A dimension is not merely another field in a database. It can be a new axis of inquiry... So dimensions can open new regions of the knowledge space.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues a dimension can function as a new axis of inquiry (Person -> Relationship -> Duty -> Consequence -> Ideal -> Action) that opens new regions of an infinite knowledge space, rather than being merely a static database field.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Relationship is first-class rather than being reduced prematurely to the same [Entity,Dimension,Value] structure.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues Relationship should be treated as a first-class KnowledgeOS construct distinct from Dimension/Statement/Value, rather than being collapsed into the same triple structure, since relationships carry their own type, context, evidence, and epistemic status.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Consequences are derived statements rather than primitive dimensions ... Inference(S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_n) \rightarrow S_{derived} ... KnowledgeOS must be able to tell the Knower: 'This is directly observed' versus 'This is inferred from three observations.'
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues consequences/inferences (e.g. 'Arjuna may kill Bhishma' derived from grandfather/opponent statements) are derived statements produced by an Inference function over prior statements, not primitive dimensions -- and that this distinction is required for evidence provenance (observed vs. inferred).

## Rationale
Argues Arjuna's Selection S was not merely adding new selected dimensions but restructuring relationships among existing ones (Enemy alone becoming Enemy-intersect-Relative-intersect-Teacher-intersect-Elder), supporting the principle NewKnowledge -> Reinterpretation(ExistingKnowledge), with the earlier 'Enemy' representation reframed as incomplete rather than false (a Zero-Lens-style move). [S0765] Argues a dimension can function as a new axis of inquiry (Person -> Relationship -> Duty -> Consequence -> Ideal -> Action) that opens new regions of an infinite knowledge space, rather than being merely a static database field. [S0766] Argues Relationship should be treated as a first-class KnowledgeOS construct distinct from Dimension/Statement/Value, rather than being collapsed into the same triple structure, since relationships carry their own type, context, evidence, and epistemic status. [S0768] Argues consequences/inferences (e.g. 'Arjuna may kill Bhishma' derived from grandfather/opponent statements) are derived statements produced by an Inference function over prior statements, not primitive dimensions -- and that this distinction is required for evidence provenance (observed vs. inferred). [S0768]
